audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 21, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for famine theology, Saul's attempted destruction of Gibeonites, treaty obligations, descendant punishment, David's selection of seven men, Mephibosheth's exemption, Michal/Merab textual issue, execution and corpse exposure, Rizpah's vigil, delayed burial, aging and battlefield fatigue, giant traditions, Goliath contradiction, and polydactyly.

verses.restored: There was famine in days of David, three years, year after year. David sought face of YHWH. YHWH said, It is because of Saul and because of house of bloodguilt, because he put Gibeonites to death.

familiar.text: Then there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David enquired of the LORD. And the LORD answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.

modern.text: During the reign of David there was a famine for three successive years, and David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, “It is because of the blood shed by Saul and his family, because he killed the Gibeonites.”

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י רָעָב֩ בִּימֵ֨י דָוִ֜ד שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים שָׁנָה֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁנָ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֥שׁ דָּוִ֖ד אֶת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל שָׁאוּל֙ וְאֶל בֵּ֣ית הַדָּמִ֔ים עַל אֲשֶׁר הֵמִ֖ית אֶת הַגִּבְעֹנִֽים

verses.restored: King called Gibeonites and spoke to them. Gibeonites were not from children of Israel but from remnant of Amorites. Children of Israel had sworn to them, but Saul sought to strike them in his zeal for children of Israel and Judah.

familiar.text: And the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them; (now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal to the children of Israel and Judah.)

modern.text: At this, David summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites, but a remnant of the Amorites. The Israelites had taken an oath concerning them, but in his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul had sought to kill them.)

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לַגִּבְעֹנִ֖ים וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְהַגִּבְעֹנִ֞ים לֹ֣א מִבְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֚י אִם מִיֶּ֣תֶר הָאֱמֹרִ֔י וּבְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נִשְׁבְּע֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם וַיְבַקֵּ֤שׁ שָׁאוּל֙ לְהַכֹּתָ֔ם בְּקַנֹּאת֥וֹ לִבְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִיהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: David said to Gibeonites, What shall I do for you, and with what shall I make atonement, that you may bless inheritance of YHWH?

familiar.text: Wherefore David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the LORD?

modern.text: So David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How can I make amends so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל הַגִּבְעֹנִ֔ים מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לָכֶ֑ם וּבַמָּ֣ה אֲכַפֵּ֔ר וּבָרְכ֖וּ אֶת נַחֲלַ֥ת יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Gibeonites said to him, There is no silver or gold for us with Saul and his house, and it is not for us to put a man to death in Israel. He said, What you say, I will do for you.

familiar.text: And the Gibeonites said unto him, We will have no silver nor gold of Saul, nor of his house; neither for us shalt thou kill any man in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that will I do for you.

modern.text: The Gibeonites said to him, “We need no silver or gold from Saul or his house, nor should you put to death anyone in Israel for us.” “Whatever you ask, I will do for you,” he replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ ל֣וֹ הַגִּבְעֹנִ֗ים אֵֽין לי כֶּ֤סֶף וְזָהָב֙ עִם שָׁא֣וּל וְעִם בֵּית֔וֹ וְאֵֽין לָ֥נוּ אִ֖ישׁ לְהָמִ֣ית בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מָֽה אַתֶּ֥ם אֹמְרִ֖ים אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: They said to king, The man who consumed us and planned against us, that we should be destroyed from standing within any territory of Israel—

familiar.text: And they answered the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the coasts of Israel,

modern.text: And they answered the king, “As for the man who consumed us and plotted against us to exterminate us from existing within any border of Israel,

original.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כִּלָּ֔נוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּמָּה לָ֑נוּ נִשְׁמַ֕דְנוּ מֵֽהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב בְּכָל גְּבֻ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: let seven men from his sons/descendants be given to us, and we will hang/expose them before YHWH at Gibeah of Saul, chosen of YHWH. King said, I will give them.

familiar.text: Let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto the LORD in Gibeah of Saul, whom the LORD did choose. And the king said, I will give them.

modern.text: let seven of his male descendants be delivered to us so that we may hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.” “I will give them to you,” said the king.

original.text: ינתן לָ֜נוּ שִׁבְעָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מִבָּנָ֔יו וְהוֹקַֽעֲנוּם֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּגִבְעַ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל בְּחִ֣יר יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲנִ֥י אֶתֵּֽן

verses.restored: King spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul because of oath of YHWH between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

familiar.text: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the LORD’s oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

modern.text: Now the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

original.text: וַיַּחְמֹ֣ל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַל מְפִי בֹ֖שֶׁת בֶּן יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בֶּן שָׁא֑וּל עַל שְׁבֻעַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֵּֽינֹתָ֔ם בֵּ֣ין דָּוִ֔ד וּבֵ֖ין יְהוֹנָתָ֥ן בֶּן שָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: King took two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and five sons of Michal/Merab daughter of Saul whom she bore/raised for Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

familiar.text: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:

modern.text: But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons whom Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul, as well as the five sons whom Merab daughter of Saul had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת שְׁ֠נֵי בְּנֵ֨י רִצְפָּ֤ה בַת אַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָלְדָ֣ה לְשָׁא֔וּל אֶת אַרְמֹנִ֖י וְאֶת מְפִבֹ֑שֶׁת וְאֶת חֲמֵ֗שֶׁת בְּנֵי֙ מִיכַ֣ל בַּת שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֛ה לְעַדְרִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן בַּרְזִלַּ֖י הַמְּחֹלָתִֽי

verses.restored: He gave them into hand of Gibeonites. They hanged/exposed them on mountain before YHWH, and the seven fell together. They were put to death in first days of harvest, at beginning of barley harvest.

familiar.text: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the LORD: and they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.

modern.text: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the hill before the LORD. So all seven of them fell together; they were put to death in the first days of the harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

original.text: וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֞ם בְּיַ֣ד הַגִּבְעֹנִ֗ים וַיֹּקִיעֻ֤ם בָּהָר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְּל֥וּ שבעתים יָ֑חַד והם הֻמְת֜וּ בִּימֵ֤י קָצִיר֙ בָּרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים תחלת קְצִ֥יר שְׂעֹרִֽים

verses.restored: Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself upon rock, from beginning of harvest until water poured upon them from heavens. She did not allow birds of heavens to rest upon them by day or animals of field by night.

familiar.text: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and suffered neither the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.

modern.text: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven poured down on the bodies, she did not allow the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.

original.text: וַתִּקַּ֣ח רִצְפָּה֩ בַת אַיָּ֨ה אֶת הַשַּׂ֜ק וַתַּטֵּ֨הוּ לָ֤הּ אֶל הַצּוּר֙ מִתְּחִלַּ֣ת קָצִ֔יר עַ֛ד נִתַּךְ מַ֥יִם עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִן הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְלֹֽא נָתְנָה֩ ע֨וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם לָנ֤וּחַ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וְאֶת חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לָֽיְלָה

verses.restored: It was told David what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, concubine of Saul, had done.

familiar.text: And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

modern.text: When David was told what Saul’s concubine Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, had done,

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לְדָוִ֑ד אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר עָשְׂתָ֛ה רִצְפָּ֥ה בַת אַיָּ֖ה פִּלֶ֥גֶשׁ שָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: David went and took bones of Saul and bones of Jonathan his son from leaders of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from square of Beth-shan where Philistines had hung them on day Philistines struck Saul at Gilboa.

familiar.text: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabeshgilead, which had stolen them from the street of Bethshan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:

modern.text: he went and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan where the Philistines had hung the bodies after they had struck down Saul at Gilboa.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת עַצְמ֤וֹת שָׁאוּל֙ וְאֶת עַצְמוֹת֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֔וֹ מֵאֵ֕ת בַּעֲלֵ֖י יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד אֲשֶׁר֩ גָּנְב֨וּ אֹתָ֜ם מֵרְחֹ֣ב בֵּֽית שַׁ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר תלום שם הפלשתים בְּי֨וֹם הַכּ֧וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֛ים אֶת שָׁא֖וּל בַּגִּלְבֹּֽעַ

verses.restored: He brought up from there bones of Saul and bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered bones of those who had been hanged/exposed.

familiar.text: And he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.

modern.text: So David had the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan brought from there, along with the bones of those who had been hanged.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַל מִשָּׁם֙ אֶת עַצְמ֣וֹת שָׁא֔וּל וְאֶת עַצְמ֖וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֑וֹ וַיַּ֣אַסְפ֔וּ אֶת עַצְמ֖וֹת הַמּוּקָעִֽים

verses.restored: They buried bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in land of Benjamin at Zela, in grave of Kish his father. They did all king commanded. After this Divine was entreated for land.

familiar.text: And the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was intreated for the land.

modern.text: And they buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in Zela in the land of Benjamin, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish. After they had done everything the king had commanded, God answered their prayers for the land. Four Battles against the Philistines (1 Chronicles 20:4–8)

original.text: וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אֶת עַצְמוֹת שָׁא֣וּל וִיהוֹנָֽתָן בְּ֠נוֹ בְּאֶ֨רֶץ בִּנְיָמִ֜ן בְּצֵלָ֗ע בְּקֶ֨בֶר֙ קִ֣ישׁ אָבִ֔יו וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖ה הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֵּעָתֵ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאָ֖רֶץ אַֽחֲרֵי כֵֽן

verses.restored: Philistines again had war with Israel. David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought Philistines. David became weary.

familiar.text: Moreover the Philistines had yet war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines: and David waxed faint.

modern.text: Once again the Philistines waged war against Israel, and David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines; but David became exhausted.

original.text: וַתְּהִי ע֧וֹד מִלְחָמָ֛ה לַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֨רֶד דָּוִ֜ד וַעֲבָדָ֥יו עִמּ֛וֹ וַיִּלָּחֲמ֥וּ אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וַיָּ֥עַף דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: Ishbi-benob, who was among descendants of Rapha, whose spear weighed three hundred bronze shekels and who was girded with a new sword, intended to strike David.

familiar.text: And Ishbibenob, which was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of brass in weight, he being girded with a new sword, thought to have slain David.

modern.text: Then Ishbi-benob, a descendant of Rapha, whose bronze spear weighed three hundred shekels and who was bearing a new sword, resolved to kill David.

original.text: וישבו בְּנֹ֜ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּילִידֵ֣י הָרָפָ֗ה וּמִשְׁקַ֤ל קֵינוֹ֙ שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וְה֖וּא חָג֣וּר חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: Abishai son of Zeruiah rescued him, struck Philistine, and put him to death. Then men of David swore to him, saying, You shall not go out with us again to battle, so you do not extinguish lamp of Israel.

familiar.text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the light of Israel.

modern.text: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then David’s men swore to him, “You must never again go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished.”

original.text: וַיַּֽעֲזָר לוֹ֙ אֲבִישַׁ֣י בֶּן צְרוּיָ֔ה וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ אָ֣ז נִשְׁבְּעוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁי דָוִ֨ד ל֜וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹא תֵצֵ֨א ע֤וֹד אִתָּ֨נוּ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תְכַבֶּ֖ה אֶת נֵ֥ר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: After this there was again battle with Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck Saph, who was among descendants of Rapha.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after this, that there was again a battle with the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Saph, which was of the sons of the giant.

modern.text: Some time later at Gob, there was another battle with the Philistines. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the descendants of Rapha.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַתְּהִי ע֧וֹד הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה בְּג֖וֹב עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים אָ֣ז הִכָּ֗ה סִבְּכַי֙ הַחֻ֣שָׁתִ֔י אֶת סַ֕ף אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּילִדֵ֥י הָרָפָֽה

verses.restored: There was again battle with Philistines at Gob. Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite struck Goliath the Gittite, shaft of whose spear was like beam of weavers.

familiar.text: And there was again a battle in Gob with the Philistines, where Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.

modern.text: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.

original.text: וַתְּהִי ע֧וֹד הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה בְּג֖וֹב עִם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּ֡ךְ אֶלְחָנָן֩ בֶּן יַעְרֵ֨י אֹרְגִ֜ים בֵּ֣ית הַלַּחְמִ֗י אֵ֚ת גָּלְיָ֣ת הַגִּתִּ֔י וְעֵ֣ץ חֲנִית֔וֹ כִּמְנ֖וֹר אֹרְגִֽים

verses.restored: There was again battle at Gath. There was a man of great size who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number; he also was born to Rapha.

familiar.text: And there was yet a battle in Gath, where was a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to the giant.

modern.text: And there was still another battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha,

translation_notes: The famine is attributed to Saul's bloodguilt against Gibeonites, preserving memory of an attempted treaty-breaking destruction. Modern famine, drought, crop failure, or food insecurity must never be diagnosed as punishment for hidden sin.

Gibeonites are a protected remnant whose covenant was violated. Their survival and grievance matter, but the killing of seven descendants who did not commit Saul's acts is collective punishment, not ethical atonement.
David chooses which descendants live and die, sparing Jonathan's son under one covenant while handing over others. Selective oath loyalty does not make the exchange just.

Verse 8 has a major Michal/Merab textual problem. Michal is elsewhere said to have no child; many witnesses and interpreters read Merab. The women and sons must not be treated as interchangeable dynastic inventory.
Rizpah's months-long vigil is embodied protest against execution, exposure, scavenging, and royal neglect. She compels belated burial without receiving direct speech from the king.

The claim that Divine was entreated after burial reports the narrative's theology; it must not imply that killing descendants caused rain or that sacrifice of vulnerable people repairs state violence.
David's weariness is not shameful weakness. His soldiers establish a safety boundary around an aging or exhausted leader.
The Goliath verse conflicts with 1 Samuel 17 and 1 Chronicles 20, which names Lahmi, Goliath's brother. Source seams must remain visible.
Six fingers and six toes are congenital bodily variation, not monstrosity, evil, or proof of nonhuman identity.
The repeated 'giant' battles are warrior traditions and may not support ethnic hatred, ableism, body-based moral judgment, or glorification of killing.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not use famine to blame communities, execute descendants for ancestors, or call exposed bodies an acceptable payment to Divine. Center the Gibeonites' violated treaty and Rizpah's protest while refusing collective punishment. Do not stigmatize aging, fatigue, unusual height, polydactyly, or other bodily difference.
